parts.text:
Outcome: Depression cases (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: benefit
Claim: Depression was associated with increased likelihood of vitamin D deficiency; read with vitamin D as the exposure, lower vitamin D went with more depression.
Sentence: "Diabetes type 2 (HbA1c ≥ 6.5%), depression, and obesity were significantly associated with an increased likelihood of VDD after accounting for other covariates."
Measured as: depression
Population: 216 adults recruited from randomly selected community-based healthcare settings in the UAE
Intervention: None; observational, vitamin D deficiency (serum level ≤ 30 nmol/L)
Comparator: Adults without vitamin D deficiency
Design: cross-sectional study
Sample size: 216
baseline_vitamin_d_status: below_20_ng_ml

## Study B
Found: no effect
Claim: In the RCT, vitamin C supplementation did not affect mood, including depression.
Sentence: "The vitamin C supplementation did not affect mood and serum concentrations of BDNF."
Measured as: depression (mood status)
Population: Healthy subjects with inadequate serum vitamin C (<50 μmol/L), n = 46
Intervention: Vitamin C 500 mg twice a day for 4 weeks
Comparator: Placebo
Design: randomized controlled trial
Sample size: 260
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

{
  "rationale": "Study B evaluates vitamin C supplementation rather than vitamin D, making the pair off-question.",
  "verdict": "off_question",
  "reason": null,

  "detail": "exposure: vitamin C supplementation"
